---

The resource plan covers the whole project. It lists the resources that actually do
the work and nothing else — a plan padded with resources that never appear on the
programme is not a plan.

Every resource below is assigned to at least one activity in
`Underground_Shelter_Final_Works_Programme.xml`; there are **426 assignments across
33 resources**. Peak numbers are the maximum simultaneous requirement and the entry
says what drives that peak.

| **Structural Consultant** | visiting | 1 | Attends the reinforcement hold points — carried from the R0 schedule | 6 |

The **structural consultant** attends the reinforcement hold points. That practice
is carried over from the supplied R0 schedule, where 'Structural Consultant
Checking' appears before each major pour, and it is retained because on a blast
structure the pre-pour inspection is the last moment at which a detailing error
can be corrected.

## Resources for the sentry post, including the brick masonry

The sentry post is an independent structure with 118 working days of float, which
makes it the natural place to absorb labour redeployment when the main works are
held up. Its resource requirement is modest and mostly sequential.

| Work | Resources | Quantity | Basis of the duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Excavation for footings F1 | Excavator, rock breaker | 37 m³ | 4 days; the rock breaker is already on site and off the main excavation |
| Blinding and footings | Concrete gang, bar bender gang | 5.4 m³ M30, 1.16 m³ M15 | Small pours, one day each |
| Columns, plinth beam, beams and slabs | Bar bender gang, carpenter gang, concrete gang | 15.6 m³ M30 | Two storeys with a 7-day cure between them |
| **Brick masonry — ground storey** | **Mason gang ×3, unskilled gang, scaffolding** | **6.88 m³ / 36.19 m²** | **5 days at roughly 2.4 m² per mason-day for a 190 wall with openings** |
| **Brick masonry — first storey** | **Mason gang ×3, unskilled gang, scaffolding** | **5.32 m³ / 28.00 m²** | **4 days; more openings, so less masonry but more cutting and more scaffold** |
| Lintels | Bar bender gang, carpenter gang, concrete gang | 0.51 m³ provisional | 2 days per storey |
| Spiral stair | Welding set, crane, unskilled gang | 1 No., 1000 R | 6 days, fabricated off site |
| Plaster | Plasterer gang ×2, scaffolding | 125 m² internal, 97 m² external | 6 days each at about 10 m² per plasterer-day |
| Flooring | Mason gang | 33 m² | 4 days |
| Electrical | Electrician gang | To be verified | Chases cut, not hammered — this is why the electrical first fix follows the masonry hold point |
| Painting | Painter gang, scaffolding | 223 m² | 6 days |

**The masonry gang is three masons plus helpers.** At roughly 2.4 m² of finished
one-brick wall per mason-day — reduced from the flat-wall rate because both storeys
are short panels between columns with a high proportion of opening perimeter and
cut brick — three masons clear the ground storey in five days and the first storey
in four. This is `[A]` and must be re-tested against the appointed contractor's
own output.

## Resource assumptions

All output rates are `[A]`. They are consistent with normal Indian site practice
and were used to build the durations in the programme, but they are the first
thing that should be re-tested when a contractor is appointed. The quantities they
are applied to are `[C]` or `[D]` and are traceable; the rates are not.
